memory_candidates.content: When a non-vacuity demonstration needs to run a modified bash script's PRE-FIX version (e.g. via `git show <commit>:path > scratch-file`) and that script sources a sibling file via `source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/common.sh"` (or similar relative-to-self sourcing), a bare extracted copy in an arbitrary scratch directory breaks immediately because SCRIPT_DIR resolves to the scratch directory, which lacks lib/. Use a temporary `git worktree add --detach <path> <commit>` instead (removed immediately after recording evidence) so the extracted script runs from its real directory structure with all sibling files present. This generalizes beyond this one script to any non-vacuity/regression demonstration against a pre-fix version of a script with relative sourcing.

When bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh (or any multi-gate full-suite verification) fails on gates unrelated to the current task's own file_scope while concurrent sibling tasks are dispatched in the same /orchestrate cycle on the same shared working tree, confirm via `git log --oneline` (for newly landed sibling commits) and `git status --short` + `diff -q <deployed> <source>` (for in-flight uncommitted sibling edits) before assuming a regression. A gate failing on a file declared in ANOTHER task's Territory file_scope, with evidence that the content/commit landed or changed during this task's own gate run, is a transient concurrency artifact, not a defect to fix inside the current task. Close the affected phase as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with a per-gate Reasoned Exclusions row (Item/Reason/Evidence) rather than redeploying repeatedly chasing a moving target that belongs to the other task.
